from: July book, night 27 (King Uzziah Grew Proud)
p1: Uzziah became king when he was only sixteen years old. He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes.
While a wise man named Zechariah lived, Uzziah looked to the Lord. As long as he did, the Lord helped him do well.
Uzziah dug many wells and loved growing things. The Lord helped him until he was very strong.
p2: But then Uzziah became proud. He felt bigger than everyone, even the Lord. He went into the temple to do a job only the priests could do. The priests said, “This is not for you, Uzziah.” But he got angry.
Jesus is never proud. He is humble, gentle and ready to listen. Tonight, cheer for someone else, the way Jesus would.
old: Uzziah became king when he was just sixteen. He loved God, and as long as he sought the Lord, God helped him do amazing things. He built towers and won battles. He became very strong and famous.
But when Uzziah got strong, he started to feel proud. He forgot that his blessings came from Heavenly Father. He thought he could do whatever he wanted, even break God’s rules.

Uzziah went into the temple to do something only the priests were supposed to do. The priests said, “Please don’t — that’s not your job!” But Uzziah got angry instead of humble. Then he got sick right away.

Pride means thinking we’re better than others and forgetting God. Heavenly Father wants us to stay humble and grateful. When we remember our blessings come from Him, we stay happy and close to God. Humble hearts please the Lord.
